title: Adaptive virtual column: live-proximity resize affordances + screenreader controls
creator: Ava Chen
description:
Problem: Our virtualized table is fast but resizing columns is error-prone and inaccessible. Users frequently overshoot or trigger accidental drags when the table is dense or when rows are virtualized (rapid reflow). We need a design that reduces accidental resizes, gives clear live feedback without hurting virtualization perf, and provides keyboard/screenreader-first controls for resizing and per-column density overrides.

Goal: Ship a unified affordance set that: (1) displays a live ‘proximity’ handle when a pointer nears a column edge, (2) shows a lightweight live preview of column width (ghost overlay) without forcing large virtualization windows, (3) exposes keyboard and ARIA controls for step-resize and density toggles, and (4) supports per-column density overrides for power users.
acceptance_criteria: Proximity handle appears when the pointer is within 8px of a column separator and disappears after 400ms idle
Live ghost overlay updates as pointer drags; overlay is rendered client-side and does not require fetching additional rows beyond current virtual window
When resize is committed, table layout updates and virtualization prefetch extends by 1 viewport in the drag direction to avoid jumpiness
Keyboard resizing: focus on column header + Left/Right arrow with Shift modifies by 10px increments; Ctrl+Arrow cycles density presets (compact / default / spacious)
Screenreader: accessible announcement of column name, current width in pixels, and available density presets; actions reachable via roving tab and single-key shortcuts
Unit/perf test: average jank measured on a 100k-row table in CI < 40ms during a resize interaction (no dropped frames on typical laptop GPU profile)
Design tokens and variable mappings for density levels added to the design system token table and referenced in the component API docs
design_notes: Proximity handle is an adaptive hit target: 8px on desktop, 14px on touch devices. Visual affordance is subtle: 2px vertical rail with 1px shadow to avoid visual noise in dense views.
Ghost overlay uses a CSS layer (position:fixed within table container) to avoid reflowing virtualized rows during drag. We avoid measuring row content mid-drag to keep CPU work minimal.
Density presets are implemented as named token sets: density-compact, density-default, density-spacious. Tokens control row-height, cell-padding, and target column-min widths.
Per-column density override is surfaced via a small badge in the header when non-default; clicking opens a mini menu with three presets.

We intentionally avoid animated layout transitions for the final commit step on low-end GPUs. Instead we fade-in the new header outline over 120ms and snap content to reduce perceived latency while preserving frame rate.
Interaction cross-browser tested in Chromium, Safari, and Firefox. Edge cases: RTL layout, frozen columns, and grouped headers considered in mockups.
decisions: Use proximity-based handle rather than always-visible drag gutters to reduce visual clutter in dense tables
Render live preview overlay in a separate composited layer to avoid expensive layout changes during drag
Keyboard resizing increments: 10px for Shift+Arrow, 1px for Arrow alone when fine-grain precision needed (but held for 200ms to avoid accidental rapid changes)
Per-column density persisted in user preferences at the workspace level (opt-in), not on the model or row level
Prefetch policy: extend virtualization buffer by 1 viewport when a user commits a resize towards offscreen content; do not prefetch during pointer hover to limit network work

qa_steps: 1) Load 100k-row dataset in the table staging app. Confirm proximity handle appears within 8px and is usable.
2) Drag handle to resize; confirm ghost overlay tracks cursor and final commit snaps content without visible reflow glitches.
3) Focus header and use Arrow/Shift/Control combos to resize and cycle density; verify announcements in VoiceOver / NVDA.
4) Verify per-column density persists across reloads for the workspace when enabled in preferences.
5) Test on Safari iPad touch profile and ensure touch hit-target is 14px and not causing accidental scroll changes.
rollout_plan: Step 1: Feature behind flag in ui-kit canary (default off) for integration testing
Step 2: Opt-in beta for 5 internal teams + collect UX telemetry for 2 weeks
Step 3: Gradual rollout to 25% of production accounts with dataset size gating (enable only for >1k rows to avoid noise)
Step 4: Full release and documentation update; announce in release notes and changelog
accessibility_considerations: Provide ARIA attributes: role=columnheader, aria-colindex, aria-label for resize handle, aria-live region for width changes
Single-key shortcuts documented and discoverable in header help menu; ensure no conflict with browser defaults
Test with VoiceOver, NVDA, and TalkBack; provide alternative UI for users who rely on keyboard-only interactions
Ensure color/contrast of proximity handle and density badge meets AA for small UI elements
migration_notes: Existing tables will default to density-default; if users had custom column widths persisted by older clients, prefer preserving explicit widths where possible
Storage change: add optional per-column density metadata to workspace settings. Migration script to set existing tables to density-default unless user-level override exists
